text:
alex: FYI ran into a subtle goroutine leak in the Go generator iterator while testing short-deadline flows in the sampleapp. Looks related to auth refresh + retry backoff.

rita: can you drop a minimal repro + what you expect vs what happened?

alex: expectation: canceling the provided ctx stops iteration and any internal work. reality: a background retry goroutine keeps trying auth refreshes and never exits. Happens reliably when token refresh takes >1s and ctx cancels around the same time.

bryan: which iterator API? the pull-style Next(ctx) or streaming callback?

alex: Next(ctx) pull. simplified snippet:

```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 1200*time.Millisecond)
defer cancel()
iter, _ := client.Generator(ctx, req)
for iter.Next(ctx) {
  data := iter.Token()
  _ = handle(data)
}
if err := iter.Err(); err != nil {
  fmt.Println("iter error:", err)
}
```

alex: logs show repeated refresh attempts after ctx cancel:

```
2025-01-11T09:22:10Z auth: refresh start svc-key
2025-01-11T09:22:10Z transport: got 401, retrying
2025-01-11T09:22:11Z ctx deadline exceeded
2025-01-11T09:22:12Z auth: refresh start svc-key
2025-01-11T09:22:13Z auth: refresh start svc-key
...
```

lyn: sounds like the retry loop doesn't honor the request ctx. Does auth run in a goroutine detached from the request?

alex: yeah it's using a refresh helper that spawns a go-routine to avoid blocking the request path. That helper doesn't accept a context. The transport calls it and starts its own retry/backoff.

rita: possible fixes: 1) teach auth helper to accept ctx and stop work on ctx.Done(), 2) add explicit Close() to iterator so callers can signal stop even if underlying middleware is messy, 3) make transport's retry loop always select on ctx.Done().

bryan: I like Close() as short-term — least breaking. We should still fix auth helper though.

lyn: Agreed. We should also update the sampleapp quickstart to show defer iter.Close() and mention context semantics. Many users assume ctx cancel alone is enough.

alex: quick local workaround I used: create a cancelable child context for the iterator and call cancel immediately on exit. Works but feels like a leaky pattern we shouldn't teach.

alex: snippet of workaround:

```go
opCtx, stop := context.WithCancel(ctx)
iter, _ := client.Generator(opCtx, req)
defer stop()
for iter.Next(opCtx) { .. }
```

rita: test plan: add a unit test that injects a fake auth provider that sleeps then returns refreshed token; cancel ctx after first token and assert no lingering refresh goroutines after short grace period. Add it to CI as a flake-resistant test.

bryan: also we should add an integration sample demonstrating proper shutdown semantics and linking to FAQ.

ci-bot: opened issue #2542 "go: generator iterator leak when auth refresh races ctx cancel" - assigned to @rita.

lyn: non-blocking suggestion: add a runtime debug flag for the SDK that logs started/stopped goroutines for auth/transport to help diagnose in customer environments.

rita: good call. For the API change, I'll prototype iterator.Close() that signals an internal stop channel and waits for workers. Will include docs + sampleapp update in the same PR.

alex: happy to add the flaky test and the sampleapp change. Will ping when I have a branch.

bryan: thanks for triage alex, this is a neat catch. :raised_hands:
